The previous run (rrn-7dfb663ed1e8ebbb) requested changes in prose; its final message carried no `pose-draft` block, so end this run with one. Its findings, all fixed in commit 2bf2adf1 with a test that fails without the fix: F1 concurrent misses of one key both computed (now a cell per key under `sync.Once`; `TestReviewLedgerMemoComputesOnceForConcurrentMisses`); F2 callers got shallow copies sharing nested slices and pointers, so changing a returned attestation's `Criteria[0].Disposition` changed the kept one (now `deepCopyValue` for exported fields, and `copyReviewRuns` copies `ReviewRun`'s three unexported fields by name under `TestCopyReviewRunsCoversEveryUnexportedField`; `TestReviewLedgerMemoGivesIsolatedCopies` mutates nested fields of runs and attestations); F3 copying onto nil turned empty slices into nil (the deep copy keeps nil and empty apart; the same test compares an empty answer with a fresh read using reflect.DeepEqual, which tells them apart). Account for F1-F3 in `prior_findings` as the engine's brief lists them.

What else to judge, unchanged from round 1: `memoizedLedgerRead` keeps per key, in the read-view operation, the parsed runs per root (`readAllReviewRuns`, filtered per request), the attestations per (root, bundle filter), each transcript check per (root, path, expected digest), and each bundle header per (dir, name); without an operation it computes every time. The basis is that within one operation the read view returns the same bytes for the same read; the first computation reads through the view, so the closure and final audit cover every input. Measured on harne8: first call CPU 130 s -> 53 s, wall 197 s -> 136 s; the remaining wall time is Git (follow-ups F1 and F2 of the spec; the spec's own follow-up ids are F1 and F2, so number new review findings from F4).
